answer: An applicant does not buy a name; they leave a witness. A uniquely serialled copper coupon is bolted to a marked reef piling and left seventy-two hours while a sealed logger's measurement kernel signs hourly conductivity, temperature, and tilt. That signed trace, with a close-up of the coupon's mill marks, is posted as a slashable bond. Reusing the same mill marks, or pulling the logger early, rejects the seat and burns the bond. A hundred identities therefore cost a hundred coupons, a hundred boat trips, three days of exposure, and every bond that fails the kernel.
